title: Polynomial joint first-order differential projective invariants
summary: We study polynomial absolute and relative joint first-order differential projective invariants for configurations of $n$ points in the plane. The main approach is based on passing to a homogeneous vector--covector representation, which reduces the problem to the classical invariant theory of the group $SL(3,\mathbb C)$. The algebra of polynomial absolute invariants is described and shown to be generated by cyclic invariants.
